title: Client microbatching and emission-smoothing for trace sampling to reduce tail overhead
creator: Sana Patel
description: Problem: At high QPS tenants we observe excessive CPU and network overhead in the tracing hot path due to immediate span emission combined with tail-based sampling decisions. This increases p99 latency and raises cost for both the SDK and ingestion pipelines. Goal: Implement a lightweight client-side microbatching layer with emission-smoothing and deferred decision windows so that tail-sampling and reservoir selection can be done with low allocation overhead and without impacting request latency guarantees. The change should minimize hot-path allocations, avoid added mutex contention, and be opt-in per SDK version and per-tenant flag.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end p99 tracing hot-path CPU overhead reduced by >= 30% for top 10 tenants in canary
Network calls for trace ingestion reduced by >= 25% under steady-state workloads (measured in events/sec)
No increase in application request p99 latency beyond existing SLOs during canary rollout
Integration tests cover microbatch windowing, backpressure, and deferred emit correctness
Feature flag exists to globally disable client microbatching per tenant and SDK version
design_decisions: Client-side microbatch buffers will be bounded circular buffers sized by span count per connection to avoid unbounded memory growth
Buffering window defaults to 50ms with adaptive backoff up to 250ms under low throughput; windows are configurable via SDK/API
Emission smoothing uses jittered timers and token-bucket rate limiter to avoid synchronized spikes across clients
Sampling hints (score, latency estimate, error flag) are attached as compact sidecar metadata to spans to enable early lightweight prefiltering without full encoding
Avoid intrusive locks: use per-thread or per-coroutine buffers with atomic pointers and an async flusher to minimize contention
Tail-sampling decisions remain server-side; clients send compact prefilt hashed keys to allow late-binding decisions with smaller payloads
migration_plan: Phase 0: Library feature flag gated, disabled by default. Instrument internal services with the new SDK build in a canary cluster
Phase 1: Enable for non-critical internal tenants at low percentage (5%) and run synthetic loadtests comparing baseline vs microbatching
Phase 2: Enable for high-volume tenants with per-tenant throttles and monitor key metrics for 72 hours
Phase 3: Roll out to all tenants with monitoring guardrails and automatic rollback on regressions
Fallback: If backend tail-sampler cannot consume compact hints, an opt-out header will force immediate emission
rollout_plan: Deploy SDK changes to canary services on runtime-1.22 cluster
Launch a 2-week canary (5% traffic) with extended metrics collection and heap/CPU profiling
Incremental ramp to 25% then 75% with automated checks; full rollout contingent on SLO gates
Post-rollout: run a 7-day cost analysis and rollback if no cost improvement observed
dashboards_to_update: Console > Tracing > Hotpath overview (add microbatch metrics and buffer heatmap)
Console > Reliability > Tail-sampler health (expose compact-hint hit-rate)
Per-tenant cost breakdown dashboard (show ingest delta pre/post rollouts)
Runtime metrics dashboard: per-process allocation and GC incidence for SDK consumers

2026-01-05: Prototype microbatcher implemented in SDK branch; integration tests added for backpressure scenarios (Miguel)
2026-01-22: Load test in canary cluster (5% traffic) shows 33% reduction in emit_calls/sec and no p99 regression; minor GC blip observed on 1% of hosts
2026-02-03: Security review concluded no sensitive data leakage in compact hints; team approved non-blocking rollout
2026-02-10: QA: intermittent ordering anomaly found when buffer flush coincides with process shutdown; added graceful drain step to SDK init/teardown
2026-02-15: Preparing rollout to high-volume tenants with additional telemetry retention enabled for 72h
notes: This approach trades a small bounded delay for substantial cost and CPU savings. Not suitable for customers requiring immediate span availability for debugging unless opt-in is disabled
We will maintain compatibility with existing trace schemas; compact hint schema v1 is backwards compatible and versioned
Follow-on work may include server-side acceptance filtering that leverages microbatching signals to improve reservoir placement
